stems.text: Three different things share one name. Hyaluronic acid. The kind your body makes, the kind in your serum, and the kind a doctor injects.
Same name, different careers?
Completely.
Like three cousins named Rahul at the same wedding.

And the mix-up costs people money, because they buy a serum expecting what an injection does. A serum is not filler in a bottle. Start in nineteen thirty-four. Karl Meyer and John Palmer pulled an unknown substance out of the vitreous, the clear jelly inside a cow's eye, and named it hyaluronic acid.
Someone looked into a cow's eyeball and thought, this could be a forty-dollar face serum?
Not immediately.
Good. That would have been unsettling foresight.
Your body already makes it. Most of it sits in your skin, where it holds water. It also lubricates your joints, and it is still doing its job inside your eye.
So, part sponge, part cushion.

That is a useful simplification. In a serum, molecular size decides almost everything. Large chains mostly stay near the surface and form a hydrating film. Smaller ones may travel farther into the upper layers of skin. Neither one behaves like an injectable filler.
Then why does my bottle say plumping?
Because hydrated surface cells can temporarily make fine lines appear softer.
So it is plumping the way watering a tired houseplant is plumping.

Yes. Not like adding a new branch. And here is the part the marketing skips. Hyaluronic acid binds water and holds onto it. It does not manufacture water out of nothing. A complete formula still needs something that stops that water leaving.
So buying hyaluronic acid without thinking about the rest of the moisturiser is hiring a lifeguard for an empty swimming pool.

Strange image. Correct principle. A filler is chemically different. Its chains are cross-linked into a gel that holds its own shape. That gel is then placed beneath the skin, where it can physically add volume.
So a filler is not just face serum with a needle?
Absolutely not.
Please put that sentence in very large letters.
That is the F D A's own wording, not ours. Dermal fillers are a medical procedure with real risks, including tissue death, vision loss and stroke. Choose a provider trained to perform the injection.
Body version, resident. Serum version, moisturiser. Filler version, construction project.
Same ingredient family. Different size, different structure, different location, so a different result. That is the entire story.
And it started in a cow's eyeball.
You waited the whole video to say that again.
